sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, and risk generally rises as utilization climbs.
The steepest rise comes at high utilization, where the contribution to default risk jumps once utilization passes about 0.74 of the credit limit.
Past delinquencies are the second or third most important driver, and having any delinquency on file raises default risk compared with having none.
Income is also an important driver, with higher income lowering default risk, although the data do not settle whether its importance is moderate.
Length of credit history has a weak to moderate effect, with longer histories associated with somewhat lower default risk.
Debt-to-income ratio, number of dependents, months at address, age and recent credit inquiries each hardly matter for the model's predictions.
The interactions in the model are small, and the data do not show that any of the pairs we examined changes the effect of one feature depending on the other.
